$comment: Vendored WHO SMART Guidelines L2 Digital Adaptation Kit sources.
The bytes are committed rather than fetched at build time, for the same reason the EDLIZ 2025
reference bundle is: a clinical rule has to be able to cite the exact document it came from,
years later, from a checkout, with no network. A URL is not a citation — it is a promise that
someone else will keep a file unchanged.
'ref' records the branch that was resolved; 'commit' is the actual pin. Note that smart-anc and
smart-fp use 'master' — raw URLs against 'main' 404, which costs an hour if you assume otherwise.
'sha256' is what makes a WHO republication visible. When fetch-dak-sources.sh sees a changed
hash it writes alongside as .incoming rather than overwriting, because a new DAK edition is a
clinical review event, not a dependency bump. The rules whose source text actually moved are
then identified by check-dak-traceability.sh, so review is scoped to what changed rather than
LICENCE: WHO publications are typically CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO. 'licenceReviewed' is false on every
entry and must stay false until someone with authority has checked the non-commercial clause
against how this platform is deployed. Reproducing WHO tables inside a shipped product is not
obviously covered, and the MEC transcription in particular reproduces substantial tables.

sources.title: WHO SMART Antenatal Care — L2 core data dictionary
sources.notes: Carries ICD-11, ICD-10, LOINC, SNOMED and ICHI codes per data element — the terminology binding comes free with the dictionary and does not need re-deriving.

sources.title: WHO SMART Antenatal Care — L2 decision-support logic and schedules
sources.notes: ANC.DT.01-38 across 16 tabs (several tabs carry a range of tables) plus ANC.S.01-05. Also contains one stray family-planning table, FP.LO.004 'reasonably certain not pregnant', which matters because the FP DAK ships no decision logic at all.

sources.title: WHO SMART Antenatal Care — L2 indicator table
WHO SMART Antenatal Care — L2 test cases
sources.notes: WHO's own fixtures for its decision tables. Where a national adaptation keeps a WHO row unchanged, the WHO fixture should pass against our engine — that is a stronger check than a fixture we wrote ourselves.

sources.title: WHO SMART Family Planning — L2 core data dictionary
sources.notes: Data elements only. THE FAMILY PLANNING DAK PUBLISHES NO MACHINE-READABLE DECISION LOGIC — input/pagecontent/cql holds a single zero-byte example. The medical eligibility criteria and selected practice recommendations therefore have no DAK artefact to cite and must be transcribed from the publications, which is why the MEC matrix is double-entry transcribed rather than extracted.

sources.title: WHO SMART Postnatal Care — L2 core data dictionary
sources.notes: Published as a versioned path rather than from a public repo, so the version string is the pin and the hash is the proof.

sources.title: WHO SMART Postnatal Care — L2 decision-support logic and schedules
sources.notes: PNC.*.DT.1-19 (suffix a = the woman, b = the newborn) plus PNC.S.01-02. The 2025 format adds a Hit Policy row and per-row rule ids, both absent from the 2021 ANC workbooks. KNOWN UPSTREAM DEFECT: PNC.S.01 publishes inverted comparison bounds for contacts 1 and 2 and its overdue column appears shifted by one; the extractor preserves them verbatim and flags them, and our schedule states the corrected window as an explicit adaptation. Worth reporting upstream.

sources.title: WHO SMART Self-monitoring of blood pressure in pregnancy — L2 core data dictionary
WHO SMART Self-monitoring of blood pressure in pregnancy — L2 decision-support logic
sources.notes: Three tables: contextual data, health actions, danger signs. Small, and load-bearing for the home blood-pressure escalation path where a reading arrives from a woman's own device rather than a clinic.
